table_assessment.assessment_notes: Continuation of the guideline-summary table with fourteen normative rows across pregnancy, chronic kidney disease, cancer, spinal cord injury, ventricular assist devices, and peripheral arterial disease. One row also contains a possibility-qualified factual hazard assertion. The table duplicates disease-specific recommendations and is not an independent table example.

header_path: Recommendations for exercise in chronic kidney disease

normative_assertions.notes: All exercise modes and dose parameters are retained in the exact target span.

text_units.verbatim_text: Low- to moderate-intensity aerobic exercise training (up to 150 min/week), and low- to moderate-intensity resistance exercise training (2 day per week, 8–12 exercises, 12–15 repetitions), and flexibility exercises are recommended in all individuals with CKD.

header_path: Recommendations for exercise in chronic kidney disease

normative_assertions.notes: Against recommendation for either stated comorbidity.

text_units.verbatim_text: Among patients with established osteodystrophy/osteoporosis, or coagulopathies, participation in contact sports is not recommended.

header_path: Recommendations for exercise in chronic kidney disease

normative_assertions.notes: All six alternative circumstances are preserved.
source_trigger_texts: is not recommended in the following circumstances

text_units.verbatim_text: Participation in sport is not recommended in the following circumstances: electrolyte abnormalities, recent changes to the ECG, excess inter-dialysis weight gain, changing or titration of medication regimen, pulmonary congestion, and increasing peripheral oedema.

entities.surface_form: Regular exercise during and after cancer therapy
quality of life, physical fitness, and prognosis

header_path: Recommendations for exercise in individuals with cancer

normative_assertions.notes: Stated purposes are normative outcomes, not separately asserted causal facts.

text_units.verbatim_text: Regular exercise during and after cancer therapy is recommended to reduce cancer-related fatigue, and improve quality of life, physical fitness, and prognosis.

header_path: Recommendations for exercise in individuals with cancer

text_units.verbatim_text: Among individuals treated with cardiotoxic medications, echocardiography before participation in high-intensity exercise is recommended.

entities.surface_form: participation in 20 min of moderate- to vigorous-intensity aerobic exercise at least 3 times a week, along with moderate-intensity resistance training 2–3 times per week
cardiorespiratory fitness, cardiometabolic health, and muscle strength benefits

header_path: Recommendations for exercise in individuals with spinal cord injury

normative_assertions.notes: Both exercise modalities, doses, and stated benefits are retained.

text_units.verbatim_text: In adults with spinal cord injury participation in 20 min of moderate- to vigorous-intensity aerobic exercise at least 3 times a week, along with moderate-intensity resistance training 2–3 times per week, is recommended for cardiorespiratory fitness, cardiometabolic health, and muscle strength benefits.

factual_relations.notes: The source says the boosting methods can be life-threatening; modality is represented as POSSIBLE.

header_path: Recommendations for exercise in individuals with spinal cord injury

normative_assertions.notes: Normative prohibition is kept separate from the possibility-qualified factual hazard.

text_units.verbatim_text: Artificial methods of inducing autonomic dysreflexia by causing intentional pain to the lower half of the body ('boosting') through obstruction of an indwelling urinary catheter, overly tight leg straps and electrical shocks or other methods of pain to the genitalia or lower limbs can be life-threatening and are not recommended.

individuals with a ventricular assist device (VAD)

header_path: Recommendations for exercise in individuals with ventricular assist devices

text_units.verbatim_text: Regular exercise, through cardiac rehabilitation, combining moderate-intensity aerobic and resistance exercise, is recommended in individuals with a ventricular assist device (VAD).

entities.surface_form: Sports that may potentially affect any of the VAD components (e.g. with body contact)

header_path: Recommendations for exercise in individuals with ventricular assist devices

normative_assertions.notes: Potential VAD-component impact defines the prohibited sport category.

text_units.verbatim_text: Sports that may potentially affect any of the VAD components (e.g. with body contact) are not recommended.

entities.surface_form: regular exercise (at least 150 min/week of moderate aerobic exercise or 75 min/week of vigorous aerobic exercise or a combination thereof)

header_path: Physical activity and sports recommendations in patients and athletes with peripheral arterial disease

normative_assertions.notes: Alternative weekly exercise doses and prevention context are retained.

text_units.verbatim_text: It is recommended that patients with atherosclerotic PAD perform regular exercise (at least 150 min/week of moderate aerobic exercise or 75 min/week of vigorous aerobic exercise or a combination thereof) as part of the secondary prevention strategy.

entities.surface_form: supervised exercise training programmes including walking to the maximal or submaximal distance for at least 3 h/week

header_path: Physical activity and sports recommendations in patients and athletes with peripheral arterial disease

normative_assertions.notes: The guideline's indicated wording is preserved as an advisory for-recommendation.

text_units.verbatim_text: In patients with symptomatic LEAD, supervised exercise training programmes including walking to the maximal or submaximal distance for at least 3 h/week are indicated.

entities.surface_form: athletes with traumatic or non-traumatic PAD following recovery after successful open surgery or percutaneous revascularization

header_path: Physical activity and sports recommendations in patients and athletes with peripheral arterial disease

normative_assertions.notes: Continuation depends on recovery after successful surgery or revascularization.

text_units.verbatim_text: Continuation of competitive sports is recommended in athletes with traumatic or non-traumatic PAD following recovery after successful open surgery or percutaneous revascularization.
